reason: The resident time window covers the recorded nine-hour sweep: native viewport-interaction on the 22-source fixture gives pan 0/120, zoom 0/24 and time 0/18 loading, so continuous_weather is true and the gate is 11/11. Two consecutive native runs after the fix gave identical numbers. A forecast-time change inside the window is served from the resident field store: the time phase decoded nothing (zero decoded-band misses), and the interval crossings published no new field images. The window holds six members over the declared nine-hour horizon in 24.5 MB of the 128 MiB store ceiling with no evictions, so the sweep fits the declared budget and no blocker is recorded.

profile.note: Unchanged from the #66 profile: the resident time window reuses the same staging path, so the per-window cost is unchanged.

resident_time_window.horizon_source: the recorded sweep moves the forecast instant over nine hours (camera.time + (i % 9) hours); the window holds the demand windows of the forecast instants inside that span
resident_time_window.member_shape: one singleton at every selection event and one bracket between two events, over one spatial window
resident_time_window.anchor: the demand's interval start; the anchor is kept while the demand stays inside the horizon, so a time change inside the window does not re-anchor it
resident_time_window.spatial_window: the presented field's own window; every member shares that window, its geometry and its resolution
resident_time_window.fill_policy: the fill starts only where the presented field was prepared, continues only while the camera stays inside that field's window, and an interactive demand cancels it
resident_time_window.flag: --resident-time-window (GribViewportModel(resident_time_window=True)); default off, the gate harness enables it

time_window_counters.provider_field_publications_note: the eleven demand-window changes published no new field images: the window's images are published when the window is filled. The single publication is the last window member, whose preparation completed about 0.1 s into the sweep; it was published once and was not re-encoded.
time_window_counters.uploads_note: This gate has no hardware-upload counter. The provider's publication count is the observable proxy: no re-encode and no new publication happened for the forecast-time changes. The render context rebinds the newly presented interval's textures at an interval crossing; those images were already published and were not re-encoded.

run_1.note: The pan phase aborted on an empty assertion: the worker promoted a prepared field from its own thread between a camera update and the render context's publication, so the published content and the model's presented field disagreed. Fixed by giving the presented field a single owner (commit b8bca25).

targeted_validation.note: The suite is 100 tests: the 96 of the #66 record plus four new resident-window tests in the viewport file (40 in that file).

endpoint: QQuickWindow.afterRendering render-callback proxy; not presentation FPS, input-to-present or scanout

change.window_layer: GribViewportModel holds a bounded resident time window: the demand windows of the forecast instants inside a declared nine-hour horizon, over the presented field's own spatial window. Each member is the field the pipeline already stages - the singleton at a selection event and the bracket between two events - so no numerical value, mask, source order or interpolation changes.
change.decoupling_layer: A forecast-time change inside the window finds a resident field in the store and never prepares one: the spatial preparation is not invalidated by a time change, and a time change does not invalidate the window's spatial preparation.
change.fill_layer: The missing members are prepared over the presented field's window, geometry and resolution, so a member shares the spatial preparation. The fill is the lowest-priority work: it starts only where the presented field was prepared, it continues only while the camera stays inside that field's window, and an interactive demand cancels it, so spatial re-centring keeps its priority over the pan pipeline.
change.publication_layer: The window's field images are published once, when the window is filled, so a forecast-time change inside the window publishes nothing and re-encodes nothing.
change.ownership_layer: The presented field has a single owner: the render context's thread. The worker hands the prepared slot forward and the next camera update adopts it, so a publication in flight cannot disagree with the model.
change.flag: --resident-time-window on the viewport entry point, resident_time_window=True on the model; default off. The default application path does not import the viewport and is byte-identical.
change.semantics: The linear temporal blend is unchanged: the blend uniform still interpolates inside the member's own interval, and an event instant is still a singleton with the exact-time mask. The recorded numerical, mask, source-order and selection tests pass unchanged.

limits: The 0/18 time result is stable across two consecutive native runs (runs 2 and 3) with identical phase numbers.

The last window member completed about 0.1 s into the sweep; the margin to its demand (input 7, 233 ms) is about 0.13 s. The fill had 0.94 s of work and the anchored-zoom phase offers about 0.9 s, so the margin is thin and a slower fill would show loading inputs.

The window is filled in the background, so a sweep that starts before the fill finishes can still show a loading input at the member that is missing; the demand outside the resident window shows an accurate loading state and then correct content.
No direct hardware-upload measurement: the provider's publication count is the observable proxy, and the render context rebinds the newly presented interval's textures at an interval crossing.
The horizon is a workload property of the recorded nine-hour sweep; a longer sweep needs a longer horizon and more retained bytes, bounded by the 128 MiB store ceiling.
Visual fidelity remains failed/user-deferred, not rerun or passed.
